result: PvCSP repeat peptides are intrinsically disordered in solution with minimal secondary structure. CD spectroscopy and MD simulations demonstrate that PvCSP peptides lack stable secondary structure, exist as large conformational ensembles, and display transient β-turns with propensities varying between VK210 and VK247 strains.
evaluation: Claims C22-C26 are well-supported by complementary experimental (CD spectroscopy) and computational (MD simulations) data. The CD spectra show characteristic minima at ~200 nm indicative of disorder (C22), MD simulations confirm large conformational ensembles (C23), and quantitative analysis of secondary structure propensities is provided (C24-C26). The methods are appropriate and the conclusions are consistent across techniques.

result: PvCSP peptides behave as harmonic springs with elastic moduli of ~3-5 cal/(mol Å²). MD simulations demonstrate that the stretching/compressing of peptides is proportional to applied force, with excellent fits (R²=0.91-0.97) to quadratic energy functions.
evaluation: Claims C27-C28 are supported by MD simulation data showing excellent fits to harmonic spring models. The elastic modulus calculations are quantitative with error estimates, and the R² values indicate robust fits. The methodology for calculating elastic properties from end-to-end distance distributions is appropriate for disordered peptides.

result: mAb 2F2 recognizes a conserved 10-residue core epitope (²DRA(D/A)GQPAGD¹¹) in PvCSPvk210 peptides in a coil conformation with one turn of a 310-helix. The antibody uses nine germline-encoded aromatic residues and accommodates sequence variation at position 5 (D/A) through minimal sidechain contacts.
evaluation: Claims C31-C37 are strongly supported by X-ray crystallography data from five different peptide co-crystal structures (Table 1, Figure 3). The structural data show consistent epitope recognition (RMSD 0.10-0.28 Å), detailed molecular interactions including H-bonds and buried surface areas, and explain cross-reactivity through structural analysis. The resolution ranges from 1.97-2.67 Å, providing high-quality structural information.

result: mAb 2E10.E9 recognizes an 8-residue core epitope (³GAGNQPGA¹⁰) in PvCSPvk247 peptides with micromolar affinity (0.507-1.67 μM). The antibody uses six germline-encoded aromatic residues and binds peptides in a coil conformation, with longer peptides accommodating two Fabs simultaneously.
evaluation: Claims C38-C43 are well-supported by ITC binding data and three X-ray crystal structures at 2.7-3.19 Å resolution. The ITC provides quantitative affinity measurements and stoichiometry determination (C38-C39), while crystal structures reveal the molecular basis of recognition including specific residue interactions and H-bonds (C40-C43). The structural consistency across peptide variants (RMSD 0.48-1.0 Å) supports the conclusions.

result: 2E10.E9 Fabs engage in head-to-head homotypic interactions at ~146° when binding PvCSPvk247 peptides. The Fab-Fab interface is primarily germline-encoded, involves symmetric HCDR2 contacts, and contributes 949 Å² of buried surface area stabilized by five H-bonds.
evaluation: Claims C44-C48 are strongly supported by the 2E10.E9 Fab-247-2 crystal structure showing two Fabs bound to one peptide. Detailed structural analysis quantifies the interface geometry, buried surface areas, H-bonds, and identifies the germline origin of contact residues through sequence comparison (C48, Figure 5C). The data provide molecular-level evidence for homotypic interactions.

result: mAbs 2F2 and 2E10.E9 exhibit fast association but different dissociation kinetics, with 2F2 showing ~10-fold higher affinity (0.242 μM) than 2E10.E9 (2.21 μM) for their respective full-length PvCSP targets.
evaluation: Claims C49-C51 are supported by complementary BLI kinetics data (Figure 6A,C) and ITC affinity measurements (Figure 6B,D). The two independent techniques provide consistent results regarding relative affinities and binding kinetics. The data are quantitative with appropriate replicates and fitting to binding models.

result: SEC-MALS analysis reveals high-stoichiometry complexes of Fabs bound to full-length PvCSP, with molecular weights of ~522 kDa (2F2-PvCSPvk210) and ~463 kDa (2E10.E9-PvCSPvk247), corresponding to approximately 10 and 9 Fabs per PvCSP molecule, respectively.
evaluation: Claims C52-C53 are supported by SEC-MALS data (Figure 6E) providing direct molecular weight measurements. The authors appropriately note slight discrepancies between ITC and SEC-MALS stoichiometry estimates and attribute this to concentration measurement challenges and different experimental conditions. The data demonstrate high-avidity binding consistent with multiple epitopes in the repeat region.

result: EM analysis reveals that 2E10.E9 Fabs bind tightly to PvCSPvk247 but do not form regular spiral assemblies, while 2F2 Fabs binding to PvCSPvk210 results in conformationally heterogeneous complexes, suggesting the central repeat region remains flexible.
evaluation: Claims C54-C57 are supported by negative stain and cryo-EM data (Figure 6—figure supplement 1). The 2D class averages show distinct binding patterns for the two antibodies. The inference that 2E10.E9 cannot form spiral assemblies due to head-to-head interactions (C55) is logical given the crystal structure data. The conformational heterogeneity observed for 2F2 complexes is directly evident in the EM classes.

result: EM analysis of 2F2 Fab bound to peptide 210-10 shows high angular flexibility (30-170°) between adjacent Fabs, indicating minimal stabilizing inter-Fab contacts. This contrasts with other CSP-targeting antibodies (2E10.E9, 3D11, 1210) that form homotypic interactions and show lower flexibility.
evaluation: Claims C58-C60 are supported by EM data (Figure 7) showing distinct 3D class distributions. The 2F2 complex displays four classes with variable angles, while antibodies known to form homotypic interactions show one or two distinct classes. The comparison to previously characterized antibodies (C60) provides appropriate context and strengthens the conclusion about the absence of extensive Fab-Fab contacts in 2F2.

result: Despite substantial sequence differences between PvCSP, PfCSP, and PbCSP repeats (different amino acid composition and repeat lengths), all three exhibit intrinsic disorder in solution. The elastic properties of PvCSP likely stem from its low-complexity periodic sequence and particular amino acid composition.
evaluation: Claims C64-C67 are supported by MD simulation data for PvCSP and comparison to published data for PfCSP and PbCSP. The sequence comparisons (C65-C66) are factual and well-documented. The inference about elastic properties (C67) is reasonable given the simulation results, though it remains somewhat speculative. The comparison across species strengthens the generalizability of findings.

result: PvCSP peptides have glycine and proline contents (22-33% and 7-11%) that place them in the transition region between amyloidogenic and elastomeric proteins. Their elastic modulus (~3-5 cal/(mol Å²)) is comparable to human elastin (~9 cal/(mol Å²)), suggesting conformational disorder may be essential for CSP function.
evaluation: Claims C68-C71 are well-supported by sequence analysis and comparison to established protein classification schemes (Rauscher et al., 2006). The elastic modulus comparison to elastin is quantitative and appropriately referenced. However, C72 is more speculative—while the analogy is reasonable, the claim that disorder is 'essential' for function goes beyond the data presented and would require functional studies.

result: mAbs 2F2 and 2E10.E9 induce coil conformations with isolated turns in PvCSP repeat peptides, similar to antibody-induced conformations observed for PfCSP and PbCSP. Both antibodies are cross-reactive within their respective PvCSP strains, binding different repeat motifs with similar affinity and identical conformations.
evaluation: Claims C75, C76, C79, C97, C98 are supported by X-ray crystallography showing consistent peptide conformations across multiple structures and ITC data demonstrating similar affinities for variant peptides. The comparison to PfCSP and PbCSP antibodies (C76) is appropriately cited. Cross-reactivity is directly demonstrated by structural and binding data for multiple peptide variants.

result: Both 2F2 and 2E10.E9 use germline-encoded aromatic residues for CSP recognition, with 2E10.E9's H.Trp50 forming interactions analogous to IGHV3-33 H.Trp52 in human anti-PfCSP mAbs. This suggests CSP repeats prime the immune system to select antibodies with optimally positioned germline aromatic residues.
evaluation: Claim C83 is well-supported by structural data and comparison to published human antibody structures. However, C84 is more speculative—while the pattern of germline aromatic residue usage is consistent across species, the inference about immune system 'priming' is a hypothesis rather than a directly demonstrated result. The claim is reasonable but goes beyond the data.

result: mAb 2E10.E9 displays head-to-head homotypic Fab-Fab interactions similar to previously described anti-PfCSP and anti-PbCSP antibodies. Unlike some other homotypic antibodies, 2E10.E9 uses primarily germline-encoded residues for Fab-Fab contacts and does not show increased affinity for longer peptides, suggesting homotypic interactions are ubiquitous among anti-CSP mAbs.
evaluation: Claims C85-C88 are well-supported by crystal structure data and sequence analysis showing germline origin of contact residues. The comparison to other antibodies is appropriately cited. However, C87 (lack of length-dependent affinity increase) is based on ITC data that shows relatively modest differences, and C89 (ubiquity of homotypic interactions) is an inference from limited examples. The conclusion is reasonable but somewhat overstated.

result: mAbs 2F2 and 2E10.E9 recognize core epitopes of 10 and 8 residues, respectively, similar to epitope lengths recognized by potent anti-PfCSP and anti-PbCSP mAbs (8-10 residues) despite different repeat lengths. This similarity suggests that similar CSP-based vaccine design approaches could be applied across Plasmodium species.
evaluation: Claims C92-C93 are well-supported by structural data and appropriate comparisons to published antibodies. However, C94 is speculative—while the structural similarities are real, the inference about vaccine design applicability is a hypothesis that would require experimental validation. The suggestion is reasonable but goes beyond what the data directly demonstrate.

result: mAbs 2F2 and 2E10.E9 are not cross-reactive between PvCSP strains VK210 and VK247 due to significantly different sequences. The lack of Plasmodium species cross-reactivity suggests that different vaccines or multicomponent CSP-based vaccines will be required for broad coverage.
evaluation: Claim C80 is supported by sequence comparison and cited literature (Nardin et al., 1982). However, C95 is a speculative inference about vaccine requirements based on limited antibody examples. While the logic is sound, the conclusion about vaccine design needs is not directly demonstrated by the data and represents a hypothesis for future testing.

result: Only mAb 2F2 induces aberrations in sporozoite size and DNA content, indicating a distinct mechanism of attenuation possibly due to higher affinity and slower dissociation compared to 2E10.E9. The affinity difference may partially stem from 2E10.E9 having fewer somatic hypermutations (1 HC, 6 KC) compared to 2F2 (14 HC, 4 KC).
evaluation: Claim C81 is supported by citation to Roth et al., 2018, but the mechanistic link to binding kinetics is speculative. Claim C82 is an inference correlating somatic hypermutation levels with affinity differences, which is plausible but not directly demonstrated. The relationship between somatic hypermutation and affinity is complex and cannot be definitively established from this comparison alone.

result: Recent in vitro experiments demonstrate that PbCSP repeats have elastic properties that are lost when the sequence is scrambled, and biophysical properties of CSP repeats are necessary for maintaining sporozoite motility.
evaluation: Claims C73-C74 are appropriately cited from Balaban et al., 2021 and Coppi et al., 2011. These are prior work claims that provide context for the current study's findings about PvCSP elasticity. The citations appear accurate based on the descriptions provided.

result: NANP homotypic antibody interactions promote activation and strong clonal expansion of PfCSP-reactive B-cells, possibly emerging from B-cell receptor clustering. However, a direct link between homotypic interactions in soluble antibodies and sporozoite inhibition remains to be established.
evaluation: Claim C90 is appropriately cited from Imkeller et al., 2018. Claim C91 acknowledges uncertainty about the functional significance of homotypic interactions for sporozoite inhibition, which is an appropriate caveat. These are contextual claims from prior work that frame the significance of the current findings.

result: Malaria caused an estimated 409,000 deaths in 2019, with the majority of cases attributed to P. falciparum and P. vivax. P. vivax is predominant outside Africa and can cause debilitating disease including fever, anemia, and adverse pregnancy outcomes.
evaluation: Claims C1-C4 are background information appropriately cited from WHO reports and published literature. These establish the public health significance of the research but are not novel findings of this study.

result: CSP is the most abundant protein on Plasmodium sporozoites and is necessary for parasite development. The PvCSP central region contains strain-specific nonapeptide repeats (GDRA(A/D)GQPA for VK210, ANGAGNQPG for VK247) that are longer than PfCSP/PbCSP repeats and consist primarily of glycine and alanine with ~26% charged residues.
evaluation: Claims C5-C10 are well-established background information appropriately cited from published literature. The sequence composition analysis (C9-C10) is factual and provides important context for understanding the structural studies.

result: VK210 and VK247 strains have worldwide distribution, with VK210 being a major target of humoral immunity. The CSP central repeat is immunodominant, and antibodies targeting it can inhibit infection. CSP-based vaccines are in clinical development, and a positive association between anti-PvCSP repeat antibodies and protection has been established.
evaluation: Claims C11-C18 are background information appropriately cited from published literature. These establish the rationale for studying anti-PvCSP antibodies but are not novel findings of this study.

result: mAbs 2F2 and 2E10.E9 were generated in mice after immunization with radiation-attenuated Pv sporozoites and significantly reduce sporozoite infectivity. mAb 2F2 at low concentrations induces aberrations in sporozoite size and DNA content, indicating post-invasion inhibition of liver stage development.
evaluation: Claims C19-C21 are appropriately cited from Nardin et al., 1982 and Roth et al., 2018. These provide important context about the antibodies studied but represent prior work rather than novel findings of this manuscript.
